chunks: And as for that which was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Ibn Udhaynah from Bukayr ibn A'yan and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) that they said:
In the male slave, he does not have the right of divorce except with the permission of his master.

So it does not contradict the first report, because his saying (peace be upon him): 'he does not have divorce except with the permission of his master,' can be understood to mean if his wife is a slave belonging to his master, rather than being a free woman or a slave belonging to someone other than his master.

And the first report has already included the specification of that, so giving preference to it is more appropriate, because the later report is like the general statement that requires clarification.
And indicating that is also what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: Does a male slave need his master's permission to divorce his wife?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction by interpreting the requirement for the master's permission as specific to the case where the slave's wife is also owned by that same master, thereby distinguishing it from other marital scenarios. This approach treats the latter narration as a general statement requiring the specific clarification provided by the former, reflecting the Shia scholarly principle of reconciling texts through contextual specificity rather than conflict. The ruling underscores the unique legal status of the 'abd' within the patriarchal and property-based family structure of the time.
